short_description: Cold desert mountain valley situated high in the Himalayas, housing millennium-old Buddhist monasteries.

description: Dharamshala is situated on the lower slopes of the Dhauladhar range. It is divided into lower Dharamshala and upper McLeod Ganj, serving as the residence of the 14th Dalai Lama and headquarters of Tibetan culture in exile.

description: Founded in 1577 by Guru Ram Das, the fourth Sikh Guru, Amritsar is the preeminent spiritual and cultural center of the Sikh faith. It is home to Sri Harmandir Sahib (the Golden Temple), Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial, Gobindgarh Fort, and the world first Partition Museum.

name: Patiala
short_description: Former capital of the Patiala princely state, renowned for Sikh palace architecture, classical music, and gardens.
description: Founded in 1763 by Baba Ala Singh, Patiala was the premier princely state of Punjab. It is renowned for the mud-and-brick Qila Mubarak fortress complex, the Patiala Gharana of Hindustani music, Phulkari embroidery, and the NIS sports institute.

name: Anandpur Sahib
short_description: Sacred town founded in 1665 by Guru Tegh Bahadur, site of the creation of the Khalsa Panth in 1699.
description: Nestled between the Shivalik foothills and Sutlej River, Anandpur Sahib (City of Bliss) is one of the five Takhts of Sikhism. It is renowned for Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib and the world-renowned Virasat-e-Khalsa museum designed by Moshe Safdie.

name: Jaipur
short_description: Capital of Rajasthan, famous for pink terracotta facades, Amber Palace, Hawa Mahal, and Jantar Mantar.
description: Founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, Jaipur was designed on Vastu Shastra principles by Vidyadhar Bhattacharya. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage City in 2019, it features Amber Fort, City Palace, Hawa Mahal, and Jantar Mantar.

name: Udaipur
short_description: Historic capital of the Mewar kingdom, famous for Lake Pichola, City Palace, and island palaces.
description: Founded in 1559 by Maharana Udai Singh II, Udaipur is situated around Lake Pichola, Fateh Sagar, and Swaroop Sagar. It features the massive City Palace complex, Jag Mandir, and Saheliyon-ki-Bari.

name: Agra
short_description: Imperial capital on the Yamuna River, renowned for the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Fatehpur Sikri.
description: Agra served as the imperial capital of the Mughal Empire under Akbar, Jahangir, and Shah Jahan. It is home to three UNESCO World Heritage Sites: the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Fatehpur Sikri, along with the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah.
